finding: The approved 256 MiB encoded bound was exhausted during the 200-request vLLM warmup. A 268432601-byte partial trace contains 9378287 records; its last record predates the measured window. No final observation is valid from this run.

proposed_change.scope: vLLM direct-CUPTI nominal encoded output bound per process only
proposed_change.interpretation: A 4 GiB per-process physical encoded-byte cap. Preserve the existing lossless codec, all activity classes, process isolation, and capture across startup, warmup, and the approved measured window.
proposed_change.rationale: The 256 MiB cap filled in about 36 seconds of activity, before measurement. Linear extrapolation of that observed rate over the approximately 240-second workload suggests about 1.8 GiB, so 4 GiB provides about a twofold buffer. This is only a planning estimate; a repeat on hardware must verify the full trace without drops or bound exhaustion.
proposed_change.failure_rule: A missing final status, stop acknowledgment, terminal frame, complete 2200-request result, per-process coverage, or zero-drop counters remains partial or failed. Preserve every failed attempt and do not resize the bound silently.
proposed_change.storage_and_cost: A complete direct-CUPTI trace could exceed 1 GiB per repetition; verify disk space and archive/download cost before each trial, and retain hashes. The exact size and incremental cost remain unknown until a bounded repeat.

required_validation_before_final_observa: implement the revised bound in only the vLLM direct-CUPTI command builder and focused CPU tests
verify the changed command against the approved W4 setpoints and unchanged vLLM request workload
run one isolated full-workload capacity preflight with the 4 GiB bound and require all 2400 requests accounted for, stop ACK, finalized traces, decoded record counts, and zero drops
download and verify every artifact before pausing the one paid instance
complete remaining trusted Nsight coverage and operational hardware gates
review exact helper source and binary hashes before final observations
